newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia, Bulgaria sign customs accord - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia, Bulgaria sign customs accord - agency.

text.p: Yugoslavia and Bulgaria signed a customs cooperation agreement on Wednesday which is expected to streamline customs formalities and have a positive effect on bilateral trade, state news agency Tanjug reported.

The agreement lays down a wide basis for cooperation between Yugoslav and Bulgarian customs services which will help each other in the implementation of customs regulations, the federal information ministry was quoted as saying.

It is a continuation of a former customs cooperation accord signed by the two countries in Belgrade on April 7, 1964. The old agreement will automatically become invalid once the new accord is ratified by the two parliaments.

The agreement particularly defines combatting illegal trade of "special" goods such as weapons, ammunition, explosives, transport of objects of historical and artistic value, drugs and toxic substances and dangerous materials.
It also deals with the transport of goods subject to high customs duties.
The two countries' customs services will establish regular contacts and direct links between central and local services for combatting smuggling and violations of customs regulations.
The accord was signed by directors of the two countries' customs agencies Mihalj Kertes and Elka Vladov.
